item.title: Trump says 'we win' regardless of Iran talks outcome
item.description:
President Donald Trump declared Saturday that the outcome of historic peace talks with Iran is of no consequence to the United States, telling reporters outside the White House that "whether we make a deal or not makes no difference to me" because "regardless of what happens, we win."

His remarks came as Vice President JD Vance led hours of negotiations with Iranian officials in Islamabad, Pakistan — the first direct high-level talks between Washington and Tehran since the 1979 Islamic Revolution.

item.title: Lebanon death toll passes 2,000 as Israel-Hezbollah fighting intensifies
item.description:
Lebanon's Health Ministry confirmed Saturday that at least 2,020 people have been killed and 6,436 wounded since the country was drawn into the broader U.S.-Israel conflict with Iran on March 2, as Israeli forces showed no signs of halting operations against Hezbollah despite ongoing ceasefire negotiations between Washington and Tehran.

The grim milestone came as the Israel Defense Forces reported striking approximately 200 Hezbollah targets across Lebanon overnight Friday and into Saturday, hitting what it described as terror infrastructure and rocket launchers in support of ground operations in southern Lebanon. Hezbollah, meanwhile, continued to fire rockets and drones into northern Israel, with sirens sounding across the Galilee region and a rocket striking the city of Safed on Thursday, injuring several people.

item.title: Qatar resumes full maritime navigation Sunday amid Gulf ceasefire
item.description: Qatar's Ministry of Transport announced on Friday the full resumption of maritime navigation for all types of vessels and ships beginning Sunday, April 12, 2026, marking a return to broader normalcy after weeks of restrictions tied to the regional military crisis.

item.title: US-Iran talks collapse after 21 hours with no deal, Vance says
item.description:
Vice President JD Vance announced early Sunday that marathon negotiations between the United States and Iran ended without a peace agreement after 21 hours of talks in Islamabad, Pakistan, with Tehran refusing to accept American demands on nuclear non-proliferation. Vance said Washington had been "quite flexible" but did not receive an "affirmative commitment" from Iran on abandoning its nuclear ambitions.

The breakdown came after the highest-level face-to-face engagement between American and Iranian leaders since the 1979 Islamic Revolution. Vance led the U.S. delegation alongside special envoy Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, President Donald Trump's son-in-law, while Iran's delegation was headed by parliamentary speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf and Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi. Pakistan mediated the trilateral discussions, which began Saturday afternoon local time and stretched past dawn Sunday.

item.title: Trump warns China of 'big problems' over Iran arms
item.description: President Trump warned on Saturday that China would face "big problems" if it supplies weapons to Iran, sharpening the economic and geopolitical standoff between Washington and Beijing even as the two nations navigate fragile ceasefire negotiations in the Middle East. The remarks, made to reporters as he departed the White House, came days after Trump threatened a blanket 50 percent tariff on imports from any country found arming Tehran.

item.title: UK shelves Chagos Islands handover after Trump opposition
item.description:
The United Kingdom announced on Saturday that it has put on hold its plan to transfer sovereignty of the Chagos Islands to Mauritius, acknowledging that the deal cannot proceed without the backing of the United States, which President Donald Trump has withheld.

The bill underpinning the agreement has been pulled from the upcoming King's Speech, where the government's legislative agenda for the next parliamentary session will be set out in May, according to Sky News. The legislation had been working its way through Parliament but ran out of time, and officials confirmed it will not be reintroduced in the next session.

item.title: China unveils 10 incentives for Taiwan after historic Xi-Cheng meeting
item.description: China on Sunday announced a package of 10 policy measures aimed at boosting cross-strait exchanges with Taiwan, capping a historic visit by Kuomintang chairwoman Cheng Li-wun that included the first meeting between leaders of the KMT and the Chinese Communist Party in nearly a decade.

item.title: USS John P. Murtha returns to San Diego with Artemis II Orion capsule
item.description: The amphibious transport dock USS John P. Murtha (LPD 26) returned to Naval Base San Diego on Saturday morning carrying NASA's Orion capsule after recovering the spacecraft and its four-person crew from the Pacific Ocean following the Artemis II lunar mission.

item.title: Economists say world far better equipped for oil shocks than in the 1970s
item.description: The Middle East conflict that has sent oil prices surging in recent months has revived memories of the 1970s energy crises, yet economists say the United States and other major economies are far better equipped to weather the storm today than they were five decades ago, according to an analysis by the Associated Press.

item.title: Iran lost track of its own mines in Hormuz, NYT reports
item.description: A desperate race for crude oil is gripping global markets as the Strait of Hormuz remains effectively shut more than six weeks after Iran closed the waterway in retaliation for the US-Israeli air campaign launched on 28 February. Physical oil prices have surged to record levels, refiners across Asia and Europe are slashing output, and a two-week ceasefire announced on 7 April has done little to restore normal shipping through the world's most critical energy chokepoint.

item.title: Study finds three distinct types of black hole mergers
item.description: A team of astrophysicists has found that merging black holes detected through gravitational waves do not all form the same way. Instead, they fall into three distinct subpopulations, each bearing the fingerprints of a different cosmic origin story. The study, submitted to the preprint server arXiv on March 18, draws on data from the LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA Collaboration's latest gravitational-wave catalog, which now contains over 150 confirmed binary black hole detections.

item.title: Putin offers to mediate after US-Iran talks collapse in Islamabad
item.description:
Russian President Vladimir Putin told Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian on Sunday that Moscow stands ready to mediate between the United States and Iran, hours after marathon negotiations in Islamabad ended without an agreement and raised fears that a fragile ceasefire could unravel.

"Vladimir Putin emphasized his readiness to further facilitate the search for a political and diplomatic settlement to the conflict, and to mediate efforts to achieve a just and lasting peace in the Middle East," the Kremlin said in its readout of the call.

item.title: Trump orders naval blockade of Strait of Hormuz
item.description:
President Trump announced on Sunday that the US Navy would immediately begin blockading all ships entering or leaving the Strait of Hormuz, a sharp escalation that came just hours after marathon peace talks with Iran in Islamabad ended without a deal.

"Effective immediately, the United States Navy, the Finest in the World, will begin the process of BLOCKADING any and all Ships trying to enter, or leave, the Strait of Hormuz," Trump wrote in a post on Truth Social, according to CBS News. He said the Navy would also "seek and interdict every vessel in International Waters that has paid a toll to Iran" and begin destroying mines Iran had laid in the waterway. "Any Iranian who fires at us, or at peaceful vessels, will be BLOWN TO HELL!" he added.

item.title: Hungarians vote in election that could end Orban's 16-year rule
item.description:
Hungarians are voting on Sunday in a parliamentary election that could end Prime Minister Viktor Orban's 16-year grip on power, with record-high turnout reported in the early hours and opposition challenger Peter Magyar's Tisza party leading in most opinion polls.

Polling stations opened at 6 a.m. local time and are set to close at 7 p.m., with roughly 8 million citizens eligible to elect the 199 members of the National Assembly. By 11 a.m., turnout had reached 37.98% — the highest ever recorded at that hour and about 12 percentage points above the same point in the 2022 election, according to Hungary's National Election Office. High turnout is widely seen as favoring the opposition.

item.title: Chinese crystal breaks record in race to build nuclear clocks
item.description:
Scientists in China have created the world's first crystal capable of producing the ultraviolet light needed to power thorium nuclear clocks, a development that could one day enable submarines and deep-space probes to navigate without GPS.

The fluorinated borate compound, developed by a team led by Pan Shilie at the Xinjiang Technical Institute of Physics and Chemistry, can push laser light down to a record 145.2 nanometres — short enough to meet a critical requirement for these ultra-precise, compact timekeepers, the South China Morning Post reported. The research was published in the journal Advanced Materials earlier this year.

item.title: IRGC claims full control of Strait of Hormuz after Trump orders blockade
item.description:
Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps declared on Sunday that its naval forces have assumed full control over all maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, issuing a sharp warning to Washington just hours after President Trump announced a U.S. naval blockade of the critical waterway.

In a statement posted in Persian on X, accompanied by video footage appearing to show vessels targeted in crosshairs, the IRGC naval command said "all traffic is under the full control of the armed forces" and warned that "the enemy will become trapped in a deadly vortex in the Strait if it makes the wrong move". The declaration came as a direct response to Trump's announcement on Truth Social that the U.S. Navy would "effective immediately" begin blockading all ships attempting to enter or leave the strait.

item.title: Russia, Ukraine trade thousands of violation claims as Easter ceasefire crumbles
item.description: A 32-hour Orthodox Easter ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine fell apart within hours of taking effect, with both sides accusing each other of thousands of breaches by Sunday morning. The truce, declared by Russian President Vladimir Putin on April 9 and effective from 4 p.m. on Saturday, was intended to cover the Easter holiday through the end of Sunday.

item.title: IRGC warns military vessels near Hormuz will breach ceasefire
item.description: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps declared on Sunday that any military vessel approaching the Strait of Hormuz would be considered a violation of the fragile US-Iran ceasefire and would be met with a "firm and forceful response," escalating a standoff over the world's most critical oil chokepoint as peace talks collapsed without an agreement.

item.title: Orban concedes as Magyar's Tisza wins Hungary election
item.description:
Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orban conceded defeat on Sunday night to opposition leader Peter Magyar, whose Tisza party was on course to win a commanding majority in the country's parliamentary election, ending 16 years of uninterrupted rule by Orban's Fidesz party.

Magyar announced the victory in a social media post, saying that Orban had personally sent his congratulations on the election win, according to Euronews. Reuters reported that Orban conceded after projections showed Tisza winning a two-thirds supermajority in the 199-seat National Assembly.

item.title: UK refuses to join Trump's Strait of Hormuz blockade
item.description:
The United Kingdom confirmed on Sunday that it will not join President Donald Trump's newly announced naval blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, directly contradicting Trump's own claims that Britain was among the countries assisting with the operation.

Trump announced the blockade in a post on Truth Social hours after US-Iran peace talks in Islamabad collapsed without a deal. "Effective immediately, the United States Navy, the Finest in the World, will begin the process of BLOCKADING any and all Ships trying to enter, or leave, the Strait of Hormuz," he wrote. In a later interview with Fox News, Trump said, "The U.K. and a couple of other countries are sending mine sweepers".

That claim was swiftly rebuffed by London. A UK government spokesperson told CBS News that Britain would not be involved in the blockade and was instead "urgently working with France and other partners to put together a wide coalition to protect freedom of navigation". The spokesperson added: "The Strait of Hormuz must not be subject to tolling".
